                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> At the end of the mobility, your institution has formal procedures for recognising student mobility (good practices linked to recognition at the end of the mobility, e.g. in the use of Transcripts of Records and Grade Distribution Tables)</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records are issued in a timely manner (normally 5 weeks) to both incoming and outgoing students</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important in the recognition framework to provide Transcripts of Records in a timely manner, immediately following the mobility period. After the mobility, the receiving institution should send a Transcript of Records to the student and to the sending institution within a period stipulated in the Inter-Institutional Agreement (normally within five weeks after publication/proclamation of the student’s results at the receiving institution). It can be provided electronically or through any other means accessible to the student and the sending institution. The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should refer to the educational components agreed upon in the Learning Agreement. Grade distribution information should be included as well, either as a web link or an annex.</p><p>Following the receipt of the Transcript of Records from the receiving institution, the sending institution should automatically transfer and recognise the student’s academic outcomes successfully completed at the receiving institution, as agreed in the Learning Agreement, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The Sending Institution will provide a Transcript of Records to the student or record the results in a database or any other means accessible to the student, normally within five weeks after having received the transcript of the receiving institution. The EU official template for the Learning Agreement for studies (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm</a></p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include, where applicable, a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Where applicable, the Sending Institution should translate the grades received by the student abroad. To enable the Sending Institution to do so, it is highly important for the receiving institution to provide a clear explanation of the institutional grading system and grade distribution in the department or study programme together with the Transcript of Records. Such information can be provided either through a web link or as an annex to the Transcripts of Records. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">All credits gained by students during a period of study abroad that were specified in the final version of the Learning Agreement are automatically transferred by your institution and count towards the students' final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The sending institution should ensure that all the credits earned by the mobile student during the mobility period are recognised and counted towards the final degree, without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. The period of study abroad must be clear in the student's records and documents issued to the student (Diploma Supplement or equivalent). This is a golden rule of recognition of credit mobility within the framework of inter-institutional agreements. All the credits towards the student's degree that are earned during the mobility period and which were originally agreed on in the Learning Agreement (or a revised version to it) should be recognised by the sending HEI without the need for the student to take any further courses or exams. Learning Agreements are binding for all the parties and require that, on successful completion of the mobility period, the sending HEI recognises credits earned by the student and documents these credits in the student records, so they can be identified in a transparent way.</p><p>Upon receipt of the Transcript of Records or Training Certificates, the sending HEI should:<br>a) certify the mobile student has fulfilled all requirements stipulated in the Learning Agreement;<br>b) ensure recognition of the mobility period abroad within the time-scale and according to the conditions stipulated in the institutional recognition framework.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of incoming students include a description of or a link to the national grading system</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records from the receiving institution should include grade distribution information, either as a web link or an annex. The local grading scale should be clearly explained, with a statistical distribution of local grades, to provide transparency and understanding of grading practices at the host institution. Where applicable, use should be made of a Grade Distribution Table for the programme of study, according to the ECTS Users’ Guide (<a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/ects/users-guide/index.htm</a>).</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Transcripts of Records of outgoing students provide details of the courses taken abroad</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The Transcript of Records should ensure a transparent recognition of the study period abroad, providing details of the courses the students undertook while studying abroad, including:</p><ul><li>Component code (if any)</li><li>Component title at the Receiving Institution&nbsp; (as indicated in the course catalogue)</li><li>If the component was successfully completed by the student?</li><li>Number of ECTS credits (or equivalent)</li><li>Grades received at the Receiving Institution</li></ul><p>The EU official template for the Learning Agreement (including the Transcript of Records) is available online: <a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/opportunities/higher-education/quality-framework_en.htm&nbsp;</a>&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Grades of outgoing students are converted, if applicable, according to a fair and transparent methodology communicated before the mobility. There are more details on this in the ECTS Users’ Guide.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/standing-out-from-the-crowd-supporting-students-through-full-recognition-and-documenting-of-mobility-outcomes" target="_blank">"Standing out from the crowd" - supporting students through full recognition and documenting of mobility outcomes</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/a-common-approach-to-ects-grade-conversion-ensuring-a-fair-assessment-of-student-performance-after-study-abroad" target="_blank">A common approach to ECTS grade conversion, ensuring a fair assessment of student performance after study abroad</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">12</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q12.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution issues a Diploma Supplement</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">To all students, automatically, free of charge and in a major European language</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>This Supplement should include a record of the period of mobility under the Erasmus+ Programme. The 48 European countries taking part in the Bologna Process have agreed that each mobile graduate in their respective country should receive the Diploma Supplement (DS) automatically, free of charge and in at least one of the major European languages in addition to the national language. The HEI should issue a Diploma Supplement (or equivalent) to accompany every degree successfully completed by a student, using - where applicable - the template developed by the European Commission, the Council of Europe and UNESCO. The HEI's policy on issuing the Diploma Supplement should be published on its website.</p><p>The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm&nbsp;</a></p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">That includes a record of the mobility period(s) carried out by the student under the Erasmus+ programme</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The information contained in the Transcript of Records from the Receiving Institution should also be included in the Diploma Supplement produced by the Sending Institution (at least for Sending Institutions located in Programme Countries), with the exact titles of the components that the student has followed abroad. Alongside modules or units taken at the sending HEI, the Diploma Supplement should list recognised modules, units and/or training activities undertaken during the student's mobility period and indicate the location of these mobility activities.<br>In the case of double, multiple or joint degrees, the Diploma Supplement should indicate the name and status of the partner HEIs awarding the degree and explain the respective language(s) of instruction and examination. In addition, an explanation should be provided about the grading and classification scheme agreed by the awarding HEIs. The template for the Diploma Supplement is available at:<br><a href="http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm">http://ec.europa.eu/education/tools/diploma-supplement_en.htm</a>&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-diploma-supplement-a-tool-to-promote-international-recognition-and-transparency-of-academic-achievement" target="_blank">The Diploma Supplement – a tool to promote international recognition and transparency of academic achievement</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">13</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q13.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> Your institution promotes and recognises staff mobility</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By taking it into account in the assessment of their professional development </span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in international projects should be seen as an important aspect of the professional development of the staff and of the modernisation of the HEI and should, therefore, be considered a key component in staff evaluation practices.</p><p>The HEI should link its HR strategy to the objectives set out the internationalisation strategy for staff. For all staff who undertake a period of mobility, HR should be informed and provide support to ensure the identification of the professional development needs of the individual as well as setting out agreed career objectives for their period of mobility. This can be through prepared addendums to staff contracts or through less formal mechanisms of agreed objectives. The new objectives should become part of the normal system of staff evaluation or appraisal and be used in order to recognise the achievements of the staff during the period of mobility. This means that HR staff should be trained to ensure these additional objectives are formally evidenced and recorded in staff records and lead to other rewards and recognition.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Through, for example the reduction of the teaching load, promotion or pay rises</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>It is highly important to incentivise staff to participate in mobility activities. In order to support and encourage mobility, HEIs should provide a number of incentives to ensure that when staff return to the sending institution, they have long term career benefits. HEIs should acknowledge periods of mobility as a normal part of a career path. Staff working schedules and agreed objectives (in terms of research outputs and assessments) should be adapted to meet their new requirements. Temporary replacements should be found during the mobility period, where possible, to ensure continuity during the mobility period. Upon returning to the sending institution, incentives to maintain links with other institutions or networks should be put in place through providing the time to nurture new relationships (reduction in teaching or research loads, continued related objectives set in performance appraisals). The new objectives set with HR for the period of mobility should be ones which are explicitly recognised and rewarded through promotion, awards or pay rises. Additional cultural / language skills should be recognised as a component in any evaluation / assessment of the staff. This may be achieved by making it well-known that participation is a formal part of staff evaluation procedures, and may lead to improvements in both working conditions and promotion or broader career prospects.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose improvements to the institutional strategy for internationalisation and overarching structure, as well as for structural reform</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>One important form of recognition for staff, which is equally beneficial to the HEI is to encourage their involvement in improving internationalisation and structural reform within the institution. This includes the opportunity for staff to provide feedback into the management structures of departments and the overall institution. There should be a firm commitment - perhaps in writing - from the HEI to recognise and make use of constructive feedback as well as the appropriate forums for staff to engage with senior management to discuss their experiences and propose new ideas for improvement.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By inviting them to share new learning and teaching practices developed abroad with their peers in the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The experience of staff should be valued and shared as an inspiration to others, by, for example, organising meetings and publishing articles where the mobile participants share their experience and the impact of mobility on their personal and professional development. Where staff are involved in teaching at host institutions, new learning and teaching practices can be brought back and shared with other staff members through seminars or presentations. Staff can be supported through the administrative and academic services to understand the skills they have acquired and how best to use them within their own institution.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">By encouraging them to propose cooperation projects with their receiving organisation</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Mobile staff bring back new partners, networks and ideas which can be of significant value for the HEI. Staff should be encouraged to propose and develop new or further cooperation projects between their receiving and sending institutions. This requires time and commitment, which need to be given formally by the sending institution, including, for example, additional support to write joint proposals.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-mobility-supporting-individuals-development-and-institutional-aims-and-objectives" target="_blank">Recognition of staff mobility – supporting individuals’ development and institutional aims and objectives</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/recognition-of-staff-participating-in-erasmus-staff-mobility-actions-and-international-cooperation-projects" target="_blank">Recognition of staff participating in Erasmus staff mobility actions and international cooperation projects</a></div>
                                             </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close-text"><i class="fa fa-times fa-2x"></i><span>Close</span></div>
                </div>
            </div>
                         <div class="eche-report-full-question-wrapper">
                <div class="eche-officer-question-title-wrapper">
                    <div class="eche-report-title-icons-wrapper">
                                                 <div class="eche-report-officer-number">
                            <img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/eche-pdf/number-corner-orange-14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">

                            <div class="eche-report-officer-number-text">14</div>
                        </div>
                        <div class="eche-officer-question-icon"><img class="eche-report-question-icon" src="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/profiles/custom/eac_profile/modules/eac_eche/images/ECHE__OFFICERS_Q14.png" width="100%" height="100%" alt="Question Icon" title="Question Icon" loading="lazy">
</div>
                    </div>
                    <div class="eche-report-title-question-text-wrapper">
                        <div class="eche-officer-question"> With regards to the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</div>
                        <div class="eche-report-button-js eche-report-detail-close"><i class="fa fa-plus-circle fa-3x"></i></div>
                    </div>
                </div>
                <div class="eche-officer-question-wrapper eche-report-question-wrapper-show">
                    <div class="eche-report-border"></div>
                    <div classs="eche-officer-must">
                                                <h3>Must have</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are monitored, evaluated and disseminated as a way to improve international cooperation and mobility activities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Linked with the overall internationalisation strategy of the institution, monitoring and evaluation of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility is essential if HEIs are to learn from their experiences. Monitoring and evaluation is more than just measuring the number and types of outputs, it needs to include capturing information on the overall outcomes and experiences of the activities at the institutional and the individual level. Systematic monitoring and evaluation should therefore include more qualitative approaches, which expressly capture the experiences in a way which helps the institution to understand the added value of its involvement in these activities. Documenting and analysing the outcomes and experiences is only the first step. To learn from the approaches taken, and the benefits gained, institutions should take time to disseminate the findings of the cooperation projects and mobility periods through, for example, meetings, workshops and publications, social media, etc. These activities will embed good practice, help the institution to iteratively improve its approach and also feed back into the on-going monitoring and evaluation.</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are used systematically for the benefit of your institution, providing internationalisation at home, hence enhancing intercultural competences of non-mobile students and staff</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The outcomes and experiences of cooperation and Erasmus+ mobility have a much wider impact than just improving mobile activities. All institutions have significant numbers of non-mobile staff and students who can benefit from the international experiences of others. As part of the monitoring and evaluation processes, HEIs should consider the impact which can be specifically made on non-mobile staff and students, giving them “internationalisation at home experiences”. This includes building international competences, cultural awareness, virtual mobility opportunities, inviting international lecturers and embedding student projects with an international focus into the curricula, and providing opportunities for local students to work together with incoming mobile participants in e.g. project work, to ensure that local students benefit from the presence of mobile students at their institution. This fits with the activities of disseminating the overall outcomes and experiences of the cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility, though tailored to a different audience. It should take into account the professional development needs of the staff at the HEI and the perspectives of non-mobile students.&nbsp;</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-best">
                                                <h3>Best practices</h3>
                                                <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">The results are exploited and disseminated, by providing participants with the results of cooperation projects and Erasmus+ mobility opportunities (e.g. presentations) to share funding possibilities</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">Results of cooperation projects are made sustainable and often lead to future stronger international cooperation of the institution</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Participation in European and international cooperation projects should be undertaken in a pro-active way and fully integrated in the HEI's modernisation and internationalisation strategy. Capturing the outcomes and experiences of international cooperation, and disseminating the results provides information which can be fed back into the overall decision making processes of the HEI. These experiences can also be compared to the expected achievements set out in the original strategy documents and can be very important informers of future strategy and sustainability. The strength of the information collected lies in the institution’s approach to reflecting on the outcomes and using the information to further improve and strengthen international cooperation. Therefore the HEI needs to have mechanisms in place which provide a forum to fully reflect on the outcomes and ask questions which will improve the sustainability of international cooperation activities for the benefit of the institution. This implies strategic working groups set at a high level within the institution, whose role is to monitor and implement internationalisation based on evidence in practice</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility Erasmus+ participants have the opportunity to present their newly acquired competences</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>The study entitled ‘Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions’ showcases how mobility can contribute to the internationalisation of higher education institutions, including the impacts on teaching methods, cooperation between HEIs and perception of staff more generally. Therefore the dissemination of outcomes is an integral part of mobility projects. Good practice would be to ensure that the dissemination is built into the support measure and participants in projects and mobility actions are allocated adequate time, resources and space to disseminate their experiences and exploit project results. This includes opportunities to share new knowledge and to highlight new opportunities (including funding) which have arisen from the new relationships formed. In order to do this, HEIs should provide support functions such as web platforms to collect results or opportunities to present results at the institutional or departmental level, as relevant.&nbsp;</p>                         <span class="eche-officer-user-answer">After the mobility, the institution tracks graduates’ progress and the impact mobility had e.g. on their employability</span>
                        <h4>Guidance note:</h4>
                         <p>Learning mobility has a goal of increasing professional, social and intercultural skills in graduates and therefore ultimately improving their employability. In order to assess whether the experiences of mobility and international cooperation have led to new skills and competences, which in turn improve graduates’ opportunities, ongoing surveys of graduates (such as student satisfaction and student destination surveys) should include a question related to participation in mobility activities and its impact on their careers.</p>                      </div>
                    <div class="eche-officer-case">
                                                <h3>Case studies</h3>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/capitalising-on-the-outcomes-and-experiences-of-erasmus-activities" target="_blank">Capitalising on the outcomes and experiences of Erasmus+ activities</a></div>
                                                <div><a href="https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/eche/the-erasmus-impact-study-effects-of-mobility-on-the-skills-and-employability-of-students-and-the-internationalisation-of-higher-education-institutions" target="_blank">The Erasmus Impact Study: Effects of mobility on the skills and employability of students and the internationalisation of higher education institutions</a></div>
                                             </div>

                </div>

Build “LendLoop”: a neighborhood tool-lending board with automated workflows

Nice to have

Terms

  • Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms
  • The work is used for AI training. The change and your solution must be your own, and you must be free to license them to us

About Us:

We are a team of marketing strategists, digital innovators, life science leaders, and other professionals who are driving growth, pushing the envelope, and going above and beyond on behalf of our clients every day.

PharmaForceIQ is a real-time customer engagement platform built specifically for life sciences. We empower leaders across functions and brands with a faster, more effective way to engage healthcare professionals and patients. By streamlining real-time optichannel execution, leveraging AI, and focusing on measurable impact, we are driving a paradigm shift from sluggish, siloed customer engagement efforts to agile, data-driven strategies that deliver unmatched efficiency and tangible results.

Position Overview:

PharmaForceIQ is seeking a Senior Accountant, Business Operations to optimize our financial infrastructure and serve as a key operational partner. We are seeking a forward-thinking professional to transform our core systems—leveraging modern platforms such as Rillet ERP, Ramp, and Tabs—to drive automation, streamline workflows, and elevate commercial decision-making. Beyond core accounting responsibilities, this individual will play a pivotal role in delivering strategic insights that advance our business objectives.

Key Responsibilities:

Strategy and automation

  • Identify opportunities to automate transactional accounting work and recommend in-app agents, tools, workflows, or configurations to capture them
  • Apply AI tools to improve accuracy, speed, and insight across the finance function, from close activities to variance analysis to reporting
  • Evaluate the current finance stack and recommend improvements
  • Propose process redesigns that reduce manual effort, close time, and error rates, with a view toward scaling the function without adding headcount
  • Benchmark our processes against industry best practice and bring forward ideas the Controller and leadership can act on
  • Partner with the Controller on roadmap decisions for Rillet, Ramp, Tabs, and future finance systems

Business operations partnership

  • Partner with the delivery team on third-party spend: category tracking, vendor accruals, and spend governance inside Ramp
  • Support Ramp operations: approval workflow maintenance, category and CoA mapping, card issuance, policy enforcement, and spend reporting back to budget owners
  • Prepare monthly budget-vs-actual packages for department leads: pull actuals, map to budget, build variance detail with drivers and commentary, and distribute for review
  • Maintain operational finance reporting that ties financial actuals to business metrics (project-level spend, department budgets, vendor concentration)
  • Support order-to-cash with commercial ops: pricing and contract review, revenue setup in Tabs, customer onboarding, and billing accuracy
  • Partner with ops on vendor onboarding, SOW tracking, and contract-to-invoice workflows

Systems and process ownership

  • Serve as a functional owner on Rillet (ERP), Ramp (spend), and Tabs (billing/AR): configuration input, process design, testing, and documentation
  • Build and document repeatable processes, controls, and close checklists
  • Own the integration touchpoints across the finance stack and flag gaps or breakage

Core accounting

  • Own AR and AP end-to-end: billing, collections, cash application, vendor management, payment runs, and 1099 reporting
  • Perform monthly close activities for assigned areas: journal entries, accruals, prepaid and deferred revenue schedules, and balance sheet reconciliations
  • Prepare flux analysis and close commentary for the Controller
  • Apply GAAP in areas including revenue recognition (ASC 606), software capitalization, and accrual accounting
  • Prepare audit schedules and respond to external audit requests

Qualifications:

•5 to 7+ years of progressive accounting experience; public accounting a plus

•CPA strongly preferred (active, or sitting)

•Demonstrated experience using AI tools (in-app agents, LLMs, workflow automation) to improve accounting or finance processes

•Strong technical GAAP knowledge: revenue recognition, accruals, deferrals, prepaids, and reconciliations

•Hands-on experience owning a monthly close in a cloud ERP; Rillet, NetSuite, or Sage Intacct experience strongly preferred

•Experience with modern spend and billing platforms (Ramp, Tabs, Bill.com, or similar) and comfort owning configuration, not just transactions

•Track record of identifying and implementing process improvements and automation

•Comfort partnering with non-finance teams (delivery, ops, commercial) and translating business questions into financial answers

•Advanced Excel; comfort with large data sets, pivots, and model clean-up

•Systems-forward and curious: brings ideas rather than waiting for direction

•Bachelor's degree in Accounting or Finance required

•Pharma, SaaS, or PE-backed company experience a plus

Grafana Labs is the company behind Grafana Cloud, the fully managed observability platform trusted by more than 10,000 organizations to ensure reliability, resolve incidents faster, and optimize telemetry at scale. Built on open source and open standards and designed for interoperability across any stack, Grafana Cloud brings AI to observability and observability to AI, giving teams (and their agents) unified visibility so they can see, understand, and act on all their disparate data, wherever it lives, and move at the speed of their ambitions. This is more than just a management role—it’s your chance to build out our practice on the forefront of the observability space. You will ensure that our customers leverage the full power of our platform to meet their business needs. This is your opportunity to drive tremendous impact, influence product direction, and help set a new industry standard for technical customer success.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  • Direct the bulk of your day-to-day work based on guidance and goals from leadership, owning the planning, actions and outcomes of the region.
  • Be responsible for customer adoption, retention and expansion, owning the ongoing reporting, analysis, and escalation of your team’s engagements.
  • Partner with AMERSales leadership on customer programs, marketing initiatives and community/company events to drive adoption and expansion.
  • Work alongside your team as an executive sponsor for our most important customers to ensure success and bring grounded feedback into your operation.
  • Leveraging advanced AI tooling to the fullest extent, while prioritizing and maintaining human control and contact.
  • Develop, refine, and improve our programs and materials to bring the best experience to our customers.
  • Attract, recruit, ramp, and mentor a team of great Observability Architects from diverse backgrounds and experiences.
  • Proactively communicate with customers and internal teams to provide a feedback loop on our products and the competitive landscape
  • Work with the team to create and enhance internal and external Grafana content and enablement.

What Makes You a Great Fit:

  • 3+ years leading a team, 5+ years in the high tech industry having held customer facing and leadership roles such as TAM Manager, Customer Success Manager, SE Manager, Architect, etc.
  • Experience as a manager-of-managers, and strong leadership coaching skills.
  • Direct experience mentoring, developing people and managing performance over time.

As the Product Manager for Percona Monitoring and Management (PMM), you will own the product strategy and execution for Percona's open source observability platform for databases. You will work closely with engineering, design, product leadership, customers, and the open source community to define the future of PMM.

This is a highly technical product role. Our users are database administrators, SREs, platform engineers, DevOps engineers, cloud engineers, and developers who rely on PMM to monitor and optimize mission-critical database environments.

We're looking for someone with an entrepreneurial mindset who enjoys moving quickly, talking to customers, validating ideas early, and iterating rapidly. This is not a role where you'll spend months writing specifications before shipping. We value experimentation, pragmatism, and delivering customer value.

What Will You Do

  • Own the product strategy and roadmap for PMM, ensuring it aligns with Percona's overall product vision.

  • Work directly with customers and the community to understand their challenges, validate ideas, and identify new product opportunities.

  • Conduct market research and competitive analysis to help shape product direction.

  • Translate customer problems into clear product requirements and priorities.

  • Work closely with Engineering, Design, Documentation, Marketing, and Customer Success to deliver outstanding product experiences.

  • Prioritize features and make informed trade-offs based on customer value, engineering effort, and strategic goals.

  • Define success metrics and use customer feedback, product telemetry, and usage data to guide product decisions.

  • Collaborate closely with engineering throughout the entire product lifecycle, from discovery to release.

  • Represent PMM internally and externally through blog posts, webinars, conferences, customer meetings, and community engagement.

  • Help drive the adoption of PMM across the open source community and enterprise organizations.

What You Have Done

  • Proven success managing technical products, particularly developer tools, infrastructure, platform, or observability products.

  • Demonstrated experience shipping successful software products from idea to release.

  • Strong technical understanding of modern infrastructure, databases, cloud-native, and observability technologies, with the ability to translate complex technical concepts into product strategy and customer value.

  • Experience working cross-functionally across engineering, design, marketing, sales, and customer success.

  • Strong customer empathy with the ability to translate customer problems into products that deliver real value.

  • Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, making decisions with incomplete information, and iterating quickly based on customer feedback.

  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.

  • Fluent in English.

  • Willingness to travel occasionally for customer visits, conferences, and company events.

What Will Make You Stand Out

  • Experience with observability technologies such as Prometheus, OpenTelemetry, Grafana, Loki, Tempo, VictoriaMetrics, or similar platforms.

  • Experience with databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, or other data platforms.

  • Experience with Kubernetes, Linux, cloud-native technologies, and distributed systems.

  • Experience working with open source communities as an active contributor or community member.

  • Experience building products for developers, SREs, platform engineers, DevOps engineers, database administrators, or other highly technical users.

  • Experience defining AI-powered workflows, developer productivity tools, or AI-assisted observability experiences.

  • Experience working in startups or high-growth companies where rapid iteration, experimentation, and customer feedback drive product decisions.

  • Comfortable taking ownership and wearing multiple hats in a small, collaborative team.

  • Passion for open source and building products in close partnership with engineering and the community.

Why Percona?

At Percona, we believe an open world is a better world. Our mission is to enable everyone to innovate freely, by providing the best open source database software, support, and services. We make databases and applications run better through a unique combination of expertise and open source software built with the community for you. Our technical teams are experts in MySQL, MongoDB, PostgreSQL, and MariaDB.

Percona is proud to be a remote-only and globally dispersed workforce – we have colleagues in more than 50 countries! We offer a collaborative, highly-engaged culture where your ideas are welcome and your voice is heard.

Our staff receives generous benefits including flexible work hours and various paid time off programs, all your equipment for your remote office, funds for career development (external training, certifications, conferences), ongoing connectivity allowances, and the opportunity to participate in our equity incentive plan. We also have benefits that support a healthy work/life balance such as The Percona Adventure Team, Work-from-Anywhere, FlowDays, FryDays, and overall flexibility. We also support being socially responsible through our PAVE volunteering program and Women Transforming Technology.

If you love the idea of working with a high-growth tech company that is one of the best in the business and known globally as a leader in the open-source database space, let’s talk!

Connect with us and stay up to date on our latest news and developments by following us on LinkedIn and Twitter. We look forward to connecting with you!

About Us

Kyriba is a global fintech leader empowering CFOs and finance teams with cloud-based treasury, payments, risk management and working capital solutions. Prospects are identified through marketing campaigns as well as direct prospecting efforts from the BDR. Interaction with the prospect involves comprehensive discussions surrounding their current Treasury operations to identify their current situation, problems and pain all while positioning Kyriba’s unique business value.


About The Team

Our Business Development team services our global sales team via several BDR-Hubs in San Diego, London, Paris, Tokyo, and Singapore. The goal of our BDR leadership is to simultaneously generate the sales pipeline needed to satisfy booking targets and train, coach, and mentor Kyriba’s next generation of sellers, customer-facing support, and marketers. Our culture is goal-oriented and embodies the better parts of collaboration amongst each other as well as cross-functionally with our partners in marketing and sales.

  • Educate contacts through comprehensive discussions around their current Treasury operations and Kyriba’s product offerings.

  • Understand and qualify the prospect accordingly.
  • Nurture non-qualified prospects by offering resources and educational materials.
  • Follow-up on inquiries from marketing campaigns, online ads, events and webinars.
  • Perform high volume outbound calling activities combined with e-mail marketing.
  • Gather key information to update SalesForce.com in order to effectively prospect specified territory.
  • Enhance product knowledge through regularly scheduled training sessions and self-education.
  • Become part of a very collaborative team in terms of training and sharing education, and best practices.
  • Establish and maintain strong relationships with the sales executive in assigned territory.
  • Provide qualified sales-ready opportunities to the field sales organization to engage in our sales cycle.

What You bring:

  • 1 year+ professional work experience or sales internship preferred.
  • Fluent in English and German.
  • Must hold a Bachelor's degree or equivalent
  • Successful track record in inside sales or cold calling environment preferred.

Your wellbeing, our mission. Join a company shaping a healthier world.

GET TO KNOW US

At Wellhub we're revolutionizing workplace wellness. Our platform connects employees worldwide to the best partners for fitness, mindfulness, therapy, nutrition, and sleep—all in one simple subscription. Headquartered in NYC with team members in Europe, North America and South America, we’re on a mission to make every company a wellness company.

We believe work should be fulfilling, inspiring, and balanced. Here, you’ll find a team that values wellbeing, collaboration, and different perspectives, where passion and creativity push boundaries to create real impact. Your contributions will help shape a healthier, more balanced world for you and millions of people globally.

Join us in redefining the future of wellbeing!

THE OPPORTUNITY

We are hiring a Senior Salesforce Engineerin our Resellers Team in Brazil! This is a Remote – Brazil position, meaning you can work from anywhere within the country. Please note that this role is only open to candidates in Brazil.

As a Senior Salesforce Software Engineer, you will be responsible for analyzing and developing high-quality, scalable solutions tailored to our reseller partners. You will own the software lifecycle end-to-end, creating technical documentation, developing features, supporting UAT/homologation, and maintaining stable live operations. Additionally, you will assist partners with technical inquiries and issue resolution, driving incident analysis and root-cause fixes to ensure a robust and reliable product.

In this role, you will work in close alignment with Product Managers to translate business rules into scalable technical solutions, support the Tech Lead in key architectural decisions, and collaborate cross-functionally with other squads. By balancing trade-offs between speed and quality, you will actively contribute to fostering a healthy, collaborative, and high-performing engineering environment.

YOUR IMPACT

  • Own the architecture and development of solutions within our Salesforce platform for the Resellers squad, making design decisions that balance scalability, maintainability, and high performance.
  • Lead RFCs and PRDs, creating detailed technical documentation, setting standards, and acting as a technical reference in code and design reviews.
  • Drive end-to-end incident resolution and root-cause analysis (post-mortems) for reseller operations, converting lessons learned into long-term system stability and quality.
  • Support homologation, deployment, and live operations, actively assisting reseller partners with technical queries, troubleshooting, and issue resolution.
  • Partner closely with Product Managers and Tech Leads to align business requirements, evaluate technical trade-offs, and guide architectural choices across squads.
  • Proactively manage technical debt across the team's codebase, ensuring a clean, scalable architecture and removing roadblocks autonomously.
  • Build solutions through both declarative programming (Flows, Approval Processes) and code (Apex, LWC, Aura), adhering to SOLID principles and leveraging GitHub CI/CD pipelines.
  • Support hiring by interviewing candidates and helping spot structural inefficiencies or roadblocks within the team.
  • Roll up your sleeves and help when needed. Live the mission: inspire and empower others by genuinely caring for your own wellbeing and your colleagues. Bring wellbeing to the forefront of work, and create a supportive environment where everyone feels comfortable taking care of themselves, taking time off, and finding work-life balance.

WHO YOU ARE

  • Hands-on experience with Salesforce development (Apex, JavaScript), with a proven track record of designing, building, and maintaining scalable solutions end-to-end.
  • Strong expertise in Lightning Web Components (LWC), Aura, and Salesforce declarative automation tools (Flows, Approval Processes), alongside solid knowledge of SOLID design patterns and Git-based CI/CD pipelines.
  • Experienced in creating complete technical documentation, analyzing architectural trade-offs, and acting as a technical guide to support Tech Leads and Product Managers.
  • A collaborative team player with strong problem-solving skills, comfortable driving incident resolution, root-cause analysis, and supporting partners with complex queries to maintain product stability.
  • Proven ability to work autonomously in agile, cross-functional environments, fostering a healthy, inclusive, and collaborative team culture.
  • Strong verbal and written communicator with fluent/advanced English skills, capable of influencing technical decisions and presenting complex ideas clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.

We recognize that individuals approach job applications differently. We strongly encourage all aspiring applicants to go for it, even if they don't match the job description 100%. We welcome your application and will be delighted to explore if you could be a great fit for our team. For this specific role, please note that prior experience with Salesforce development (Apex, JavaScript) are mandatory requirements.

WHAT WE OFFER YOU

With thoughtful benefits, emotional wellbeing resources, and a culture that empowers you to take ownership of your role and your wellbeing, we create an environment where you can thrive in all dimensions of your life.

Our flexible benefits program allows you to customize some of the benefits, according to your needs!

Our benefits include:

WELLHUB: Free Gold+ membership with access to onsite gyms and studios, digital fitness programs, and online wellness resources for meditation, nutrition, mental wellbeing support, and more! Add up to three family members to your plan, ensuring access to wellness for those who matter most to you.

WELLZ: A complete emotional wellbeing program with a unique approach. It offers personalized journeys that combine individual therapy sessions (52 per year) and on-demand content.

HEALTHCARE: Health, dental, and life insurance.

FLEXIBLE WORK: As a Flexible First company, we offer hybrid and remote options to give you the freedom to work in a way that suits you. The model for this specific role can be discussed with your recruiter and hiring manager. When you join, use our home office reimbursement to set up your home office.

FLEXIBLE SCHEDULE: Flexibility for us isn’t just about where we work—it also means being able to shape how and when we get things done. Together with their leaders, employees define schedules that align with their time zones, team needs, and personal routines.

PAID TIME OFF: It’s important to take time away from work to recharge.Employees receive vacations after 6 months and additional 3 days off per year + 1 day off for each year of tenure (up to 5 additional days) + an extra holiday for your birthday!

PAID PARENTAL LEAVE: Welcoming a new child is one of the most special moments in your life. Take the time to be present and enjoy your growing family. We offer 100% paid parental leave to all new parents. Parents giving birth are eligible for an extended leave and a ramp-back period to return part-time while they get settled.

CAREER GROWTH: Access world-class platforms, participate in interactive sessions, build your personalized development roadmap, and explore internal opportunities. We focus on continuous learning and feedback to support your journey toward personal and professional success.

CULTURE: You’ll join a team of passionate people who come together to break boundaries, support each other, and create a meaningful impact in workplace wellness. We win together, building trust through open communication and a culture where every perspective matters. Learn more about our shared culture and values here.

Want to see what it’s really like to work here? Follow us on Instagram @lifeatwellhub and watch our team video on YouTube!

When our values align, there's no limit to what we can achieve.

At Parexel, we all share the same goal - to improve the world's health. From clinical trials to regulatory, consulting, and market access, every clinical development solution we provide is underpinned by something special - a deep conviction in what we do.

Each of us, no matter what we do at Parexel, contributes to the development of a therapy that ultimately will benefit a patient. We take our work personally, we do it with empathy and we're committed to making a difference.

Are you a commercially minded finance professional who enjoys turning complex financial data into decisions that make a real difference?


We are looking for a Commercial Finance Manager to join Parexel and act as a trusted financial partner to our Commercial and Operational leadership teams.

This is much more than a traditional finance role. You will work closely with senior stakeholders across the business, using financial insight, commercial judgement and scenario modelling to shape decisions, strengthen client partnerships and improve the profitability of key client portfolios.

You will become a recognised commercial finance expert for your assigned clients, bringing together financial performance, pricing, forecasting and business intelligence to help teams make informed decisions and deliver sustainable growth.


You can work remotely or in a hybrid pattern in this role, which is connected to our Dublin office - you must live in Ireland. If you work remotely, we may occasionally ask you to come into the office for Team or Client meetings, but this is not frequent.



What you’ll do:


In this role, you will:


  • Partner with Commercial, Portfolio, Business Operations and Finance leaders to improve the financial performance of key client accounts.
  • Translate complex financial and commercial data into clear, actionable insights for senior stakeholders.
  • Provide forward-looking financial analysis, scenario modelling and recommendations to support strategic decision-making.
  • Develop a deep understanding of client economics, profitability drivers, revenue, costs and margin performance.
  • Identify financial risks and opportunities across client portfolios and recommend actions to enhance profitability.
  • Challenge and influence Commercial leadership where appropriate to ensure decisions balance client needs with Parexel’s financial objectives.
  • Analyse actual and forecast performance, investigate variances and help drive corrective actions.
  • Partner with Proposals & Contracts and Commercial teams on financial analysis and pricing for proposals, including complex, multi-million-dollar opportunities.
  • Support the resolution of complex commercial finance issues, acting as a trusted escalation point where required.
  • Build strong relationships with internal stakeholders and, where appropriate, directly with clients on financial and commercial matters.
  • Support continuous improvement across Commercial Finance, helping simplify processes, strengthen financial discipline and embed best practices.

What we’re looking for:


We’re looking for someone who can combine strong financial expertise with genuine commercial judgement and stakeholder influence.


You’ll ideally bring:


  • Approximately 6–10 years of progressive Finance experience, with a strong track record in commercial finance, financial analysis or business partnering.
  • A degree in Finance, Accounting or a related discipline, with professional Accounting or Finance Qualification e.g. CIMA, ACA, ACCA or equivalent.
  • Strong financial modelling and analytical skills, with the ability to identify the story behind the numbers.
  • Experience supporting commercial decisions around areas such as pricing, profitability, forecasting, revenue and margin.
  • The confidence to challenge assumptions, influence decision-making and have constructive conversations with senior stakeholders.
  • Strong business partnering skills and the ability to build credibility with both Finance and non-Finance leaders.
  • Experience working within a complex, matrixed and ideally global organisation.
  • An ability to operate effectively when priorities are changing or information is incomplete.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial concepts clearly.
  • Experience within the CRO, pharmaceutical, life sciences or another project-based professional services environment would be particularly valuable.

What will make you successful:


You’ll thrive in this role if you naturally look beyond reporting the numbers and ask “What does this mean for the business, and what should we do next?”

You will be comfortable moving between detailed financial analysis and strategic conversations with senior leaders. You’ll understand when to challenge, when to influence and when to propose a different commercial approach.

Most importantly, you’ll be able to balance customer needs with strong financial stewardship, helping Parexel build sustainable, profitable client partnerships.


If you’re looking for a role where you can combine finance, strategy, commercial partnership and influence, we’d love to hear from you!

Job Description Summary

‎

Role Summary

The Senior Telephony Analyst serves as the primary business resource for the Five9 telephony platform supporting CareMore operations. This role is responsible for day-to-day platform administration, troubleshooting, governance, reporting, and optimization to ensure telephony capabilities effectively support business and operational needs.

The Senior Telephony Analyst partners closely with operational leaders, IT teams, vendors, and other stakeholders to translate business requirements into effective telephony solutions. The role supports auto-dialer and SMS campaigns, Workforce Management capabilities, system integrations, licensing and capacity management, and platform enhancements while using data and analytics to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.

‎

How will you make an impact & Requirements

‎

Key Responsibilities

  • Serve as the primary business resource and subject matter expert for the Five9 telephony platform across CareMore, providing day-to-day administration, troubleshooting, governance, and optimization.
  • Configure, manage, and optimize Five9 auto-dialer campaigns, including campaign setup, dialing strategies, performance monitoring, troubleshooting, and ongoing enhancements.
  • Support the development and ongoing operation of Five9 SMS campaigns, partnering with business teams on requirements, configuration, testing, troubleshooting, and optimization.
  • Develop and analyze telephony and operational reporting to identify trends, investigate performance issues, measure effectiveness, and provide actionable insights and recommendations to leaders.
  • Support integrations between Five9 and internal systems and applications, partnering with IT teams, vendors, and business stakeholders to troubleshoot issues and implement enhancements.
  • Monitor Five9 licensing, utilization, and platform capacity; identify current and anticipated needs and recommend adjustments to support operational requirements and growth.
  • Support Workforce Management capabilities, including forecasting, intraday management, reporting, configuration, and system troubleshooting in partnership with operational leaders.
  • Partner with leaders and stakeholders across CareMore to understand business requirements, recommend telephony solutions, and identify opportunities to improve workflows, productivity, and platform utilization.
  • Coordinate testing and implementation of Five9 platform changes, enhancements, and new functionality while minimizing operational disruption.
  • Develop and maintain platform documentation, configuration standards, procedures, and other resources to promote consistent and effective use of telephony capabilities.
  • Monitor platform performance and recurring issues, escalating technical concerns and coordinating resolution with IT teams and vendors as appropriate.
  • Stay current on Five9 capabilities and telephony best practices and recommend opportunities to improve the user and customer experience.

Qualifications

<p class="mt-5 whitespace-pre-line text-lg leading-relaxed text-[#526760]">You'll own the data layer underneath InsightsOS and EngageOS, the products that turn booking, CRM, ad, and financial data from multi-location brands into proactive insights and automated actions. Today that layer is built and maintained by our product lead alongside two full-stack engineers. We need someone who owns it end to end: architecture, modeling, pipelines, and the analytical models on top. You'll report to our product lead and work directly with the founder.</p>
<p class="mt-5 text-lg leading-relaxed text-[#526760]"><strong>Compensation:</strong> $45–60K plus revenue-share bonus (we profit share every month)</p>

<ul class="mt-5 list-disc space-y-3 pl-6 text-lg leading-relaxed text-[#526760]">

      <title>Current: Freelance Marketo Email Engineer</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Front-End Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote (US)
</p>

<h3>&nbsp;</h3>
<h2><strong>About the Role</strong></h2>
<p>As a Freelance Marketo Email Specialist, you'll build, test, and launch email programs in Marketo for a range of client brands. This is a hands-on, execution-only contract role with no leadership or management responsibilities. You'll take approved briefs and turn them into working programs, building responsive templates and modules, setting up smart lists and flows, and making sure every send goes out right the first time. You know Marketo well enough to spot a broken token, a misfired trigger, or a segmentation gap before it reaches a subscriber. You'll take direction from our internal team, get up to speed fast, and deliver accurate builds on schedule with minimal oversight.</p>
<h2><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></h2>
<ul>
<li>Build and launch email programs in Marketo, including one-off sends, nurture streams, engagement programs, and triggered campaigns.</li>
<li>Develop and maintain responsive email templates and modular components in HTML and CSS, using Marketo's template syntax, variables, and editable sections.</li>
<li>Set up smart lists, smart campaigns, flow steps, and segmentations that match the targeting and logic in the brief.</li>
<li>Use tokens, dynamic content, and snippets to personalize emails and keep programs easy to clone and reuse.</li>
<li>QA every email before launch: rendering across clients and devices (e.g. Litmus or Email on Acid), links, tokens, personalization fallbacks, and list logic.</li>
<li>Manage program structure, naming conventions, and folder organization so client instances stay clean and easy to navigate.</li>
<li>Build to the brief and requirements provided, and flag any gaps or errors in the request before they become problems in the send.</li>
<li>Communicate status, timelines, and blockers clearly with your internal point of contact.</li>
<li>Document builds and processes so other team members can pick up, update, or reuse the work.</li>
<li>Follow established Marketo, deliverability, and accessibility standards on every build.</li>
</ul>
<h2><strong>Qualifications</strong></h2>
<h3><strong>Required</strong></h3>
<ul>
<li>At least 3 years of hands-on experience building and deploying email campaigns in Marketo Engage.</li>
<li>Strong working knowledge of Marketo programs, smart lists, smart campaigns, tokens, snippets, and dynamic content.</li>
<li>Proficiency in HTML and CSS for email, including responsive and hybrid coding and Marketo template syntax.</li>
<li>Experience with email rendering and QA tools such as Litmus or Email on Acid.</li>
<li>A detail-oriented QA process that catches errors in logic, links, and personalization before launch.</li>
<li>Experience working across multiple clients or Marketo instances, adapting quickly to different setups and conventions.</li>
<li>Clear, proactive communication, including flagging risks early and giving accurate time estimates.</li>
<li>Ability to work independently, take direction well, and hit deadlines across overlapping requests.</li>
</ul>
<h3><strong>Preferred</strong></h3>

      <title>Clover Health: Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations</title>
      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
      <category>Full-Stack Programming</category>
      <description>

<p>
  <strong>Headquarters:</strong> Remote - USA
</p>

<p>Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention &amp; Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders.</p>
<p>This is a non-attorney role.&nbsp; You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud.</p>
<p><strong>As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention &amp; Investigations, you will:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: </strong>Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1.</li>
<li><strong>Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: </strong>Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions.&nbsp; Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure.&nbsp;</li>
<li><strong>Build Defensible Documentation: </strong>Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions.</li>
<li><strong>Collaborate Across Functions: </strong>Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact.</li>
<li><strong>Communicate Findings Clearly: </strong>Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Success in this role looks like:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>In your first 90 days</strong>, you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals.</li>
<li><strong>By 6 months</strong>, you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt.</li>
<li><strong>By 12 months</strong>, you have a track record of strong investigations, successful recoveries and/or referrals, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Senior leaders across Clover view you as a trusted person to call when they have a hunch that something doesn't look right and want it examined.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>You should get in touch if:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Knowledge of healthcare fraud schemes &amp; investigative experience: </strong>You have experience in healthcare fraud investigations, program integrity, or SIU operations, ideally within Medicare Advantage or managed care.&nbsp; You understand healthcare fraud schemes and know how to use claims data, medical records, and provider documentation to build a defensible factual record.</li>
<li><strong>You are AI-native and enjoy building things using LLMs:</strong> You can use LLMs to write SQL, Python, etc., to interrogate large claims and/or medical record datasets, automate investigative work, and prototype your own solutions rather than waiting for someone else to build them. <em>We do not expect production-grade engineering or require formal technical training—we value demonstrated ability to build, ship, and showcase solutions that work.</em></li>
<li><strong>Strong communication skills: </strong>You are a strong writer and communicator who can turn complex investigative findings into clear memos, referrals, and executive summaries, and you are comfortable building in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Bonus points if:</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>
<ul>
<li>You have built something people actually use—an internal tool, detection model, script, automation, or AI workflow that made a manual process better. We would rather see something scrappy and useful in production than something polished in a slide.</li>
<li>You have hands-on experience applying AI/ML to fraud, investigations, or compliance.</li>
<li>You have a J.D., legal training, or experience working alongside Legal, SIU, or compliance at a health plan.</li>
<li>You have industry certifications such as CFE, AHFI, or CHC.</li>
</ul>
</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<p><strong>Benefits Overview</strong>:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Financial Well-Being</strong>: Our commitment to attracting and retaining top talent begins with a competitive base salary and equity opportunities. Additionally, we offer a performance-based bonus program, 401k matching, and regular compensation reviews to recognize and reward exceptional contributions.</li>
<li><strong>Physical Well-Being</strong>: We prioritize the health and well-being of our employees and their families by providing comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage. Your health matters to us, and we invest in ensuring you have access to quality healthcare.</li>
<li><strong>Mental Well-Being</strong>: We understand the importance of mental health in fostering productivity and maintaining work-life balance. To support this, we offer initiatives such as No-Meeting Fridays, monthly company holidays, access to mental health resources, and a generous flexible time-off policy. Additionally, we embrace a remote-first culture that supports collaboration and flexibility, allowing our team members to thrive from any location.&nbsp;</li>
<li><strong>Professional Development</strong>: Developing internal talent is a priority for Clover. We offer learning programs, mentorship, professional development funding, and regular performance feedback and reviews.</li>
</ul>
<p><em>Additional Perks:</em></p>
<ul>
<li>Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) offering discounted equity opportunities</li>
<li>Reimbursement for office setup expenses</li>
<li>Monthly cell phone &amp; internet stipend</li>
<li>Remote-first culture, enabling collaboration with global teams</li>
<li>Paid parental leave for all new parents</li>
<li>And much more!</li>
</ul>
<hr>
<p><strong>About Clover: </strong>We are reinventing health insurance by combining the power of data with human empathy to keep our members healthier. We believe the healthcare system is broken, so we've created custom software and analytics to empower our clinical staff to intervene and provide personalized care to the people who need it most.</p>
<p>We always put our members first, and our success as a team is measured by the quality of life of the people we serve. Those who work at Clover are passionate and mission-driven individuals with diverse areas of expertise, working together to solve the most complicated problem in the world: healthcare.</p>
<p>From Clover’s inception, Diversity &amp; Inclusion have always been key to our success. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer and our employees are people with different strengths, experiences, perspectives, opinions, and backgrounds, who share a passion for improving people's lives. Diversity not only includes race and gender identity, but also age, disability status, veteran status, sexual orientation, religion and many other parts of one’s identity. All of our employee’s points of view are key to our success, and inclusion is everyone's responsibility.</p>
<hr>
<p>#LI-REMOTE</p>

We are an</em><a href="https://e-verify.uscis.gov/esp/media/resourcesContents/E-Verify_Participation_Poster.pdf"><em> </em><em>E-Verify</em></a><em> company.</em></p>

      <region>Anywhere in the World</region>
